summary: Backend-only testing for 'Nain Photo State — Hisab' (Hindi khata mobile app). Seeded two users in MongoDB (user_test123/testtoken123 and user_test456/othertoken456) and executed a 36-test pytest suite against the public EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. All 36 tests passed (100%). Verified auth (session/me/logout), full CRUD for customers/entries/jobs, cascade delete, strict per-user isolation, absence of MongoDB _id and user_id in responses, and Pydantic validation for enum fields. No backend issues found.
critical_code_review_comments: DELETE /api/customers, /api/entries, /api/jobs return {ok: true} even when the id does not exist or belongs to another user. This is idempotent-friendly and does NOT leak data (data isolation confirmed by test_user_b_cannot_delete_user_a_customer), but if 404 semantics on delete are desired, main agent could optionally return 404 when nothing was deleted.
POST /api/auth/session and other create endpoints return 200 (FastAPI default) instead of 201 Created. Not a bug — just a convention note.
server.py is a single 317-line file; still under the 700-line threshold, no split needed yet.
seed_data_creation: Seeded two users + sessions directly in MongoDB `test_database`: user_test123 with session token `testtoken123`, user_test456 with `othertoken456`. All TEST_-prefixed customers/entries/jobs created during the run were cleaned up in the final TestZZCleanup class.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend URL: from /app/frontend/.env EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. Seeded tokens: `testtoken123` (user_test123, test@example.com) and `othertoken456` (user_test456, other@example.com). Re-run seeding via mongosh if the sessions expire (7-day TTL) or the DB is reset. Test suite: `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_backend.py -v`. All endpoints covered: /api/auth/{session,me,logout}, /api/customers CRUD, /api/entries C/R/D, /api/jobs CRUD, cascade delete, and user isolation.
rca_of_issue: No bugs found. All auth rejection paths (missing/invalid header, invalid token, missing/invalid session_id) return 401 correctly. Cascade delete works. User isolation is enforced via {user_id: ...} filter on every query and Mongo compound indexes exist at startup.
